paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: Jesus is not worried about what we don't have. Philip counted the money and came up short. Andrew looked at a boy's lunch and asked, "But what difference will these make among so many?" (John 6:9). Both of them were doing honest math, and Jesus was already holding the answer, because John 6:6 says He "knew what He was about to do."

Now look at what Jesus does with that small lunch. He takes it, gives thanks, and everyone gets "as much as they wanted" (John 6:11). There were twelve baskets left over, so what He gives is more than enough. And when the crowd wanted to make Him king by force, He withdrew to a mountain by Himself (John 6:15). He will not be handled, friend. He is the one who gives, and nobody gets to run Him.

Then comes the dark, the wind, and a boat full of scared people. Jesus says, "It is I; do not be afraid" (John 6:20), and then they were willing to take Him into the boat (John 6:21). So when your plate looks small and your night looks stormy, bring Jesus what you have and be willing to let Him into the boat. I'm still holding on to my apron, because this story is not over.
